title: Rosalind and the Terminal
premise: Jonah Eriksen, nonbinary caretaker of the derelict Svalgard Seed Vault, has spent a decade keeping Earth's last living archive alive while running supply routes between colonies that severed contact after the Consolidation. When they intercept a distress call in Old Meridian—a language erased along with the people who spoke it—they learn that the colony of Vesper Hollow, officially 'never settled,' was massacred by Consolidation forces to seize its water rights, and every record of it purged. Pursued by Auditor-Captain Reyes, who genuinely believes Jonah is a terrorist fabricating history, Jonah races to find the massacre's surviving witness: an old woman hidden inside the vault's cryo-archive for forty years. The climax comes when Jonah decrypts the vault's sealed founding manifest—proof written in the extinct tongue—and broadcasts it on every open channel, forcing Reyes to choose between her oath and the truth; she lets the broadcast through and resigns her commission. In the end, Vesper Hollow's dead are formally remembered, the vault becomes a free archive rather than a state secret, and Jonah finally stops running.
about_author: August Whitlock is the pen name of a former archivist who spent years cataloguing records that governments would have preferred forgotten. They write science fiction about ordinary people who refuse to let the past be edited.

chapters.title: The Long Route
chapters.summary: Third-person limited POV following Jonah Eriksen as they tend the seed vault's failing climate systems and pilot their aging freighter between silent colonies. Establishes their isolation, their ritual of talking to the seeds, and the quiet grief of serving worlds that no longer answer. Emotional beat: lonely competence masking deep abandonment.

chapters.title: A Voice in Dead Tongue
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. During a routine sweep of dead frequencies, they catch a repeating distress signal in Old Meridian, a language Jonah only knows from their grandmother's forbidden songs. The signal names a place no map acknowledges: Vesper Hollow. Emotional beat: wonder curdling into dread—the past is speaking, and it is screaming.

chapters.title: What the Charts Erase
chapters.summary: Jonah deciphers fragments using grandmother's dictionary, learning the signal claims a massacre and begs for a witness. Cross-checking official Consolidation archives shows Vesper Hollow 'never existed.' First hint someone else heard the signal too: a survey ship altered course toward them. Emotional beat: vertigo of realizing reality itself has been falsified.

chapters.title: The Visitor
chapters.summary: Auditor-Captain Reyes arrives at the vault under pretense of inspection, courteous and thorough, probing about anomalous transmissions. Jonah lies for the first time in ten years. Dual-tension scene told from Jonah's POV with Reyes's controlled menace. Emotional beat: the law arrives smiling, and it is more frightening than any pirate.

chapters.title: Grandmother's Box
chapters.summary: Searching their late grandmother's effects, Jonah finds a physical key and a note in Old Meridian: 'If they come asking, the archive remembers.' The key fits a sealed sublevel of the vault Jonah was never given clearance to enter. Emotional beat: inheritance revealed—not seeds, but testimony.

chapters.title: Below the Frost Line
chapters.summary: Jonah descends into the forbidden sublevel and finds a hidden cryo-bay, one occupied pod, and decades-old logs describing the founding fleet—including ships registered to Vesper Hollow. The pod's occupant is still alive. Emotional beat: awe and terror; the vault has been hiding a person all along.

chapters.title: Mira
chapters.summary: They revive Mira Solvang, ninety-one, last survivor of Vesper Hollow, who chose forty years of cold sleep over silence. Her firsthand account of the water-rights massacre unfolds in her own voice. Emotional beat: grief made flesh; statistics become a woman with a name and burned hands.

chapters.title: Every Record Says Otherwise
chapters.summary: Reyes returns with a warrant, having traced the transmission. She presents flawless official history proving Vesper Hollow was a fiction invented by separatists. Jonah realizes evidence alone won't win—Reyes believes what she was taught. Emotional beat: despair; how do you prove a massacre to someone whose world depends on its denial?

chapters.title: The Manifest
chapters.summary: Mira reveals the founding manifest—a complete colony charter written in Old Meridian, stored in the vault's deepest core, unforgeable because its encryption predates Consolidation record standards. But retrieving it means breaking vault seals Jonah swore to protect. Emotional beat: duty inverted; protecting the archive now requires violating it.

chapters.title: Sealed Doors
chapters.summary: Jonah works through the night breaching the core, guided by Mira's memories of the vault's original builders—her own parents among them. Flashbacks braid past and present. Reyes's ship holds position in orbit. Emotional beat: intimacy across generations; the vault was always meant for this moment.

chapters.title: Interception
chapters.summary: Consolidation forces jam the vault's uplinks and demand surrender of 'the terrorist and the impostor.' Jonah transmits a partial decryption as proof of life and intent. POV alternates briefly to Reyes, who begins privately doubting the records' too-perfect consistency. Emotional beat: siege pressure; the first crack in the enemy's certainty.

chapters.title: What Reyes Was Taught
chapters.summary: A Reyes-centered chapter: her academy training, her career built on cases like this one, her dawning recognition that every 'fabricated' settlement she audited shared the same archival fingerprint. She requests verification and is stonewalled by her own bureau. Emotional beat: the corrupting weight of institutions on honest people.

chapters.title: The Witness Deposes
chapters.summary: Mira records formal testimony, naming officers, dates, and the order authorizing the massacre—which she memorized before fleeing. Jonah notarizes it against the manifest's cryptographic chain. Together they build a case no court ever asked for. Emotional beat: grim purpose; justice assembled by hand outside the law.

chapters.title: Betrayal at the Airlock
chapters.summary: A junior vault technician, coerced by Consolidation threats to his family, disables the outer locks. Boarders take the upper levels; Jonah, Mira, and the manifest retreat into the cryo-bay. Emotional beat: betrayal and its mercy—the technician leaves them a warning scrawled in Old Meridian.

chapters.title: Cold Hold
chapters.summary: Trapped at -60°C with failing power, Jonah and Mira wait out the search. Mira tells the story of the night she ran, carrying her brother's name-tag. Jonah confesses their decade of silence—choosing invisibility while others were erased. Emotional beat: mutual absolution in the dark.

chapters.title: The Broadcast Decision
chapters.summary: Jonah calculates the cost: broadcasting the full manifest will burn the vault's power reserves, risking the seed collection itself. Mira says the seeds mean nothing if the lie outlives them. Jonah decides. Emotional beat: sacrifice weighed and chosen; inheritance redefined as memory, not matter.

chapters.title: Every Open Channel
chapters.summary: Climax part one: Jonah hijacks the relay network and broadcasts the manifest, the testimony, and the distress signal's original audio on all frequencies, in both languages. Colonies that haven't spoken in years begin answering—one by one. Emotional beat: catharsis; the silenced speak simultaneously.

chapters.title: Reyes's Choice
chapters.summary: Ordered to destroy the transmitter and execute the occupants, Reyes instead verifies the manifest against her own field records, finds the forgery impossible, and stands down her squad, arresting her own orders. Climax part two. Emotional beat: a single conscience outweighing an institution.

chapters.title: Aftermath of Light
chapters.summary: Consolidation leadership disavows the operation but cannot suppress a galaxy-wide reception. Independent tribunals convene; the technician's family is freed; Mira testifies publicly, standing, without notes. Emotional beat: exhausted triumph; justice arriving late but arriving.

chapters.title: The Vault Reopened
chapters.summary: The seed vault is chartered as a free archive governed by descendant communities, including Vesper Hollow's scattered survivors. Jonah, offered directorship, hesitates—institutions corrupted everyone they've known. Emotional beat: wary hope; power offered to someone who has seen its teeth.

chapters.title: Terms of Trust
chapters.summary: Jonah accepts stewardship only under rotating oversight and an unalterable public log—building corruption-resistance into the walls. Reyes, resigned, asks to stay as an auditor of the archive against her former bureau. Emotional beat: reconciliation without naivety; trust engineered, not assumed.

chapters.title: First Planting
chapters.summary: Epilogue: spring above the frost line. Jonah plants Vesper Hollow's recovered seed stock in open ground for the first time in two centuries, Mira beside them, the manifest carved in stone at the plot's edge in both languages. The long route now runs between worlds that speak. Emotional beat: quiet renewal; the future takes root in testified soil.
